description.text: Glaukos is an ophthalmic pharmaceutical and medical technology company focused on developing novel, dropless therapies and commercializing associated products for the treatment of glaucoma, corneal disorders, and retinal disease. We first developed Micro-Invasive Glaucoma Surgery (MIGS) as an alternative to the traditional glaucoma treatment paradigm, launching our first MIGS device, the iStent, commercially in 2012. In 2024, we commenced commercialization activities for iDose® TR, a first-of-its-kind, long-duration, intracameral procedural pharmaceutical implant designed to continuously deliver glaucoma drug therapy inside the eye for extended periods of time. We also offer commercially proprietary bio-activated pharmaceutical therapies for the treatment of corneal disorders. Beyond our approved products, we continue to develop and advance a robust pipeline of novel, dropless platform technologies designed to meaningfully advance the standard of care and improve outcomes for patients suffering from chronic eye diseases. Ophthalmic diseases and disorders are a national and global health concern and, as the population ages, the number of individuals with vision impairment and blindness is increasing.

about.description_short: Glaukos ( www.glaukos.com ) is an ophthalmic pharmaceutical and medical technology company focused on developing and commercializing novel therapies for the treatment of glaucoma, corneal disorders, and retinal diseases. Glaukos first developed Micro-Invasive Glaucoma Surgery (MIGS) as an alternative to the traditional glaucoma treatment paradigm, launching its first MIGS device commercially in 2012. In 2024, Glaukos commenced commercial launch activities for iDose TR, a first-of-its-kind, long-duration, intracameral procedural pharmaceutical designed to deliver 24/7 glaucoma drug therapy inside the eye for extended periods of time. Glaukos also markets the only FDA-approved corneal cross-linking therapy utilizing a proprietary bio-activated pharmaceutical for the treatment of keratoconus, a rarely diagnosed corneal disorder.

analysis_md:
# GKOS — Glaukos Corporation
v5 run, 2026-10-20. **In scope** (market cap $9,548,442,400 at $166.96, nasdaq_quote_api — under the $40B scope cap). US GAAP filer on Form 10-K (FY2025, filed 2026-02-23). No overrides — the preliminary run had no DATA_GAP.

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json, or statements.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Ophthalmic medical technology and pharmaceuticals company (SIC 3841, 1,094 employees per profile.json) built around interventional glaucoma: the iStent MIGS family, iDose TR (sustained-release intracameral travoprost implant, launched February 2024), and Corneal Health — Photrexa transitioning to Epioxa (first FDA-approved epithelium-on corneal cross-linking therapy for keratoconus, launched 2026). Q2 2026 mix (company reporting): consolidated net sales $185.6M, +~50% YoY — U.S. glaucoma $118.5M (+64%, iDose TR ~$74M), international glaucoma $36.6M (+17%), Corneal Health $30.4M (+48%, Epioxa ~$11M in its first full quarter). Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $680M–$700M after Q2 (from $600M–$620M at the FY2025 release), with FY2026 operating expenses guided to ~$600M.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow -$14,789,000; capex $7,666,000; SBC $63,218,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: -$85,673,000 = -$1.50/share** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_latest_per_share -1.4980416156670746, base_oe_total_latest_fy -$85,673,000, shares 57,190,000). FCF was -$22,455,000 — negative before SBC is even counted.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): -$235,119,000 — far worse than the conservative figure, driven by the working-capital build (ΔNWC $77,855,000 in financials_history.csv; receivables balance rose from $60,744,000 to $108,608,000 in statements.json as iDose TR scaled). The OCF-based conservative figure is the cleaner series and it is still negative.
- OE positive **0 of the last 5** fiscal years. Per-year conservative OE/share (financials_history.csv): FY2023 -$2.51, FY2024 -$2.23, FY2025 -$1.50 — improving, still negative.
- **Base used = the normalized 3-yr median: -$2.23/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; base_oe_per_share -2.233437588854137).
- **TTM check (ttm.py, saved in ttm.json):** OCF FY -$14,789,000 − prior YTD -$11,542,000 + current YTD $2,297,000 = **TTM -$950,000**; capex FY $7,666,000 − prior YTD $3,117,000 + current YTD $6,697,000 = **TTM $11,246,000**; SBC FY $63,218,000 − prior YTD $31,005,000 + current YTD $48,009,000 = **TTM $80,222,000**; shares (current-YTD weighted diluted) 58,419,000. **TTM OE total -$92,418,000 → -$1.58/share** (ttm_oe_per_share -1.5819853129974837). The TTM base sits between the latest-FY and median bases and is also negative, so no --ttm pin was applied — the F verdict does not depend on base choice.
- Balance sheet (FY2025, financials_history.csv / statements.json): cash $90,813,000, total assets $893,487,000, total liabilities $237,332,000, equity $656,155,000, lease liabilities $37,081,000 (dcf_numbers.json). **No borrowings:** the company retired the full $287.5M principal of its 2.75% convertible senior notes due 2027 during 2024 (the FY2023 balance sheet still carried $282,773,000 of long-term debt in statements.json; FY2024 and FY2025 carry none), and the FY2025 results release reports ~$282.6M of cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments and restricted cash with **no debt**.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, category real, economics unproven
Justification: Category creator and leader in interventional glaucoma: the iStent family holds the largest MIGS share with over one million devices implanted and a deep clinical-evidence base, iDose TR is the first sustained-release intracameral travoprost implant (re-administration makes it recurring), and Epioxa is the first FDA-approved epithelium-on corneal cross-linking therapy for keratoconus. Pricing power is in the filed numbers: GAAP gross margin 76.0% (FY2023) and 75.5% (FY2024) in fundamentals.json, and ~84% non-GAAP in FY2025 (the GAAP 55.7% is a one-time $112.9M non-cash Avedro intangible impairment, not price erosion). But there is no demonstrated return on capital: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is negative in every year FY2021–FY2025 (-5.34%, -15.84%, -27.61%, -16.18%, -27.89%) and conservative owner's earnings are positive in 0 of the last 5 years. The franchise is hostage to Medicare coverage/reimbursement decisions, faces Alcon/Sight Sciences/AbbVie competition, and pays for growth with rising SBC ($63,218,000 in FY2025, $80,222,000 TTM).
- FOR: Interventional-glaucoma category leadership — iStent family is the largest MIGS franchise (over one million devices implanted worldwide, deep peer-reviewed evidence base), iStent infinite extends it to standalone use; iDose TR, first sustained-release intracameral drug implant, with re-administration creating a recurring-revenue refill model (~$74M of Q2 2026 sales, U.S. glaucoma +64% YoY); Epioxa, first FDA-approved epithelium-on cross-linking therapy (~$11M in its first full quarter, permanent J-code effective July 1, 2026); pricing power (GAAP gross margin 76.0%/75.5% in FY2023/24, non-GAAP ~84% FY2025, ~85% Q2 2026); pipeline breadth — five platforms / 13 programs plus a trained surgeon base that is costly for rivals to replicate.
- AGAINST: No demonstrated returns on capital (roic_proxy negative every year FY2021–25, OE positive 0/5 years); reimbursement is the weak wall (Medicare Administrative Contractor coverage for iDose TR still being settled, Epioxa J-code transition guided to cause Q3 2026 volatility, MIGS reimbursement cuts have reduced volumes before); competition from Alcon (Hydrus), Sight Sciences (OMNI), AbbVie (XEN) and drops/laser, with combo-cataract MIGS competition abroad baked into management's own guidance; dilution funds the franchise (SBC $43,528,000 FY2023 → $63,218,000 FY2025 → $80,222,000 TTM; diluted count compounding 6.4%/yr); concentration and execution risk (growth hinges on the iDose TR ramp and Epioxa launch while opex is guided to ~$600M for 2026).
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection. (Moot for the score — see DCF.)

## DCF — Tier F: no scenario table exists, and that is the finding
The engine's Tier F branch fired: the normalized base is not positive, so no scenarios, IVs, or IRRs are computed (implied_irr_weighted: null). Probabilities recorded for the run: 10/25/30/25/10 (defaults — nothing in the evidence justifies tilting weights for a branch that does not use them).
- **F sub-type: no_cash_generation** (f_subtype_basis: sum of the last 3 fiscal years, the median window). FCF legs from financials_history.csv: FY2023 -$78,006,000, FY2024 -$67,618,000, FY2025 -$22,455,000 — negative in sum and in every year. This is not merely the "SBC ate positive FCF" subtype: operating cash flow itself was negative in all three years (-$57,758,000 / -$61,318,000 / -$14,789,000) before capex and SBC.
- **Growth sanity check:** the engine's blended growth is 16.50% (dcf_numbers.json: rev CAGR 5y 17.67%, 3y 21.50%, latest YoY +32.33%, after the -5pp share-count adjustment). Recent prints run well above the blend — FY2025 revenue +32.33%, TTM revenue $612,839,000 at +41.55% YoY (fundamentals.json), Q2 2026 sales +~50% YoY, and FY2026 guidance of $680M–$700M implies +34–38% on FY2025's $507,442,000. Written reason, as the spec requires: every scenario start the defaults would produce (super bear 4.50% to super bull 28.50% off the 16.50% blend) sits below the latest prints because the prints are a product-launch ramp (iDose TR from February 2024, Epioxa from 2026) off a smaller base, not a steady-state rate — and decisively, growth applied to a negative base produces no valuation in any case. No growth input changes this tier.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): resolved with ttm.py, whose full output is saved in ttm.json and quoted under Owner's earnings above — TTM OE -$92,418,000 → -$1.58/share, between the latest-FY (-$1.50) and median (-$2.23) bases and negative like both, so the median base was retained and no pin applied.
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 6.4%/yr): real and structural. Diluted shares (financials_history.csv / ttm.json): 48,433,000 (FY2023) → 52,755,000 (FY2024) → 57,190,000 (FY2025) → 58,419,000 (current YTD 2026). Two drivers: SBC-funded compensation compounding (SBC $43,528,000 → $50,207,000 → $63,218,000 → $80,222,000 TTM) and the FY2024 retirement of the $287.5M convertible notes, which was partly equity-settled — additional paid-in capital rose from $1,059,751,000 (FY2023) to $1,509,831,000 (FY2024) in statements.json alongside a $18.0M exchange-charge line in the FY2024 results. The -5pp growth adjustment already deducts the trend; the point for the verdict is that any future positive OE gets divided by a count still growing ~6%/yr.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income vs operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): explained year by year from statements.json, and in each year the gap is non-cash addbacks, not cash earnings the OCF series misses. FY2023: net income -$134,661,000 vs OCF -$57,758,000 — SBC $43,528,000 + D&A $33,654,000 ≈ the whole $76,903,000 gap. FY2024: -$146,372,000 vs -$61,318,000 — SBC $50,207,000 + D&A $35,650,000 plus ~$18.0M of convertible-note exchange charges (a $17.4M non-cash inducement charge, per the FY2024 results release). ## My thoughts / overlay
- There is no method range to hide behind: normalized median base -$2.23/share, latest-FY base -$1.50/share, TTM base -$1.58/share, maintenance base far lower at -$235,119,000 on the FY2025 working-capital build. Every defensible variant is Tier F. Anyone quoting a DCF value for GKOS today is projecting the inflection, not measuring owner's earnings.
- The inflection is real on the top line and in cash trajectory: OCF improved from -$61,318,000 (FY2024) to -$14,789,000 (FY2025) to -$950,000 TTM, FCF from -$67,618,000 to -$22,455,000 to -$12,196,000 TTM (fundamentals.json), on revenue +32% (FY2025), +41.55% TTM, +~50% in Q2 2026 with guidance raised to $680M–$700M. But the same TTM shows exactly what still eats the business: SBC of $80,222,000 against OCF of -$950,000. Even at OCF breakeven, SBC alone puts owner's earnings ~$80M underwater; opex guided to ~$600M for 2026 says management is still spending ahead of the ramp.
- What would change the tier: a filed period in which OCF − capex − SBC is positive. On the current trajectory that requires OCF to clear roughly $90M+ at the current SBC run-rate — plausible on the guided revenue path if gross margin holds ~85% and opex discipline arrives, but it is not in any filed period yet. The FY2026 10-K (expected February 2027) is the refresh trigger; an H2 2026 OCF surge would show in the Q3/Q4 10-Qs first.
- Quality note for the file: an unlevered balance sheet (~$282.6M of reported liquidity, no debt), ~84–85% non-GAAP gross margins, and two scarce assets (the only sustained-release glaucoma implant; the only approved epithelium-on cross-linking therapy) are genuine franchise evidence. At $166.96 and a $9,548,442,400 market cap the price already pays for the inflection completing — there is no margin of safety measurable in OE terms, which is what this screen measures.
